name: Common Architecture Risk Patterns
description: Reusable risk patterns frequently identified in architecture assessments

riskTemplate.title: Scalability constraints due to monolithic architecture
riskTemplate.description: The current monolithic architecture may not support expected growth in users/transactions and desired deployment frequency without significant refactoring.
riskTemplate.mitigationProposal: Consider a phased decomposition strategy starting with the highest-traffic or most-changed modules. Begin with identifying bounded contexts and extracting services incrementally.

patterns.title: Single point of failure in data layer

riskTemplate.title: Single point of failure in database layer
riskTemplate.description: Reliance on a single database instance without replication or failover creates a single point of failure that risks service outage.
riskTemplate.mitigationProposal: Implement database replication with automatic failover. Consider read replicas for read-heavy workloads. Evaluate multi-region options for disaster recovery.

riskTemplate.title: Cascade failure risk due to tight service coupling
riskTemplate.description: Heavy reliance on synchronous inter-service communication creates cascade failure risk and makes independent deployment difficult.
riskTemplate.mitigationProposal: Introduce asynchronous communication patterns (event-driven, message queues) for non-critical paths. Implement circuit breakers and bulkheads for synchronous calls.

riskTemplate.title: Breaking changes risk without API versioning
riskTemplate.description: Lack of API versioning strategy means any API change risks breaking external consumers, creating upgrade coordination challenges.
riskTemplate.mitigationProposal: Implement API versioning strategy (URL path or header-based). Establish deprecation policy. Document breaking vs non-breaking change criteria.

riskTemplate.title: Operational blind spots due to insufficient observability
riskTemplate.description: Insufficient monitoring, logging, and alerting means production issues may go undetected or be difficult to diagnose, increasing MTTR.
riskTemplate.mitigationProposal: Implement structured logging, key business and technical metrics, distributed tracing, and alerting on SLO violations. Start with the most critical user-facing paths.

riskTemplate.title: Security vulnerability due to inadequate access controls
riskTemplate.description: Insufficient authentication and authorization controls expose the system to unauthorized access and potential data breaches.
riskTemplate.mitigationProposal: Implement industry-standard authentication (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC). Apply principle of least privilege for authorization. Conduct security review of all API endpoints.

riskTemplate.title: Business continuity risk without disaster recovery plan
riskTemplate.description: Absence of a documented and tested disaster recovery plan means the organization cannot reliably recover from major incidents.
riskTemplate.mitigationProposal: Define RPO/RTO targets. Implement backup strategy with tested restore procedures. Consider multi-region deployment for critical services. Document and regularly test the DR plan.

riskTemplate.title: Deployment risk and slow delivery due to manual process
riskTemplate.description: Manual deployment processes increase the risk of human error, slow down release cycles, and make rollbacks difficult.
riskTemplate.mitigationProposal: Implement CI/CD pipeline with automated build, test, and deployment stages. Start with the most critical service and expand coverage incrementally.

riskTemplate.title: Regression risk due to insufficient test coverage
riskTemplate.description: Low test coverage increases the risk of undetected regressions when making changes, reducing confidence in releases.
riskTemplate.mitigationProposal: Establish minimum test coverage targets. Prioritize testing of critical business flows. Implement test gates in CI pipeline to prevent coverage regression.

riskTemplate.title: Data loss risk without backup strategy
riskTemplate.description: Absence of automated backup and restore procedures creates risk of irrecoverable data loss in case of failure or human error.
riskTemplate.mitigationProposal: Implement automated backup with defined retention policy. Test restore procedures regularly. Consider point-in-time recovery capability.
